utterances.text: On the 25th in the evening I went to the house of my in-laws, my wife's parents, and I did not return down there any more so I could not see any of the attacks on Bradina because that is quite on the opposite side from the place where I was and the place where that was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So not on the 26th nor on 27th May were you on the scene to be able to testify to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot say anything, you were not present. You did not see people being captured or what happened to the women and children during those two days, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you have testified, on 27th May you went down to this creek to the woods with another 35 persons and there you hid for a day or two; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would not say two days. We were there for one day and then we decided next morning to go down to the road and to report ourselves in.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if you told the investigator, the prosecutors, that it was two days, it might have been a slip of the tongue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 25th to 28th in the morning I was in the area. One of those nights we spent in the creek and we slept there because the soldiers were already shooting around the place, setting houses on fire. That might have been 27th, the night of 27th. On 28th in the morning we reported it down there and we spent one night there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question in this connection. You know that Bradina, in view of the configuration of the terrain, has many remote isolated houses scattered on the nearby hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can agree with me that after these events it was quite risky to stay in these houses, for a family to stay in so lonely a place, it was quite risky, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we have done enough for this period. We will break and come back at 4.30 for you to continue. (4.00 pm) (A short break) (4.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. You may proceed, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grubac, on 28th May you surrendered to the forces of the TO, HVO and MUP who were in Bradina and who already controlled the whole territory of Bradina by that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would prefer to say that this was the Muslim and Croat army. I do not know what TO or anything else they belong to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, you surrendered to a member of the MUP called Nurko Habibija who, as you know, before the war was a traffic policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He is a Muslim, if you prefer us to talk about the ethnic background of those people, and then a Croat called Zilic, also a member of the MUP, drove you to the police station in Konjic, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who before was not a member of the MUP, if you said of Nurko that he was a member of the MUP before the war, this one was not. Yes, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Habibija or Zilic say anything to you on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Habibija said nothing and Zilic drove four of us men to Konjic. I do not recall he said anything in particular that I would remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there in the police station in Konjic you were taken to a small cell in the police building, as you have already testified in court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is so, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again from your former experience and your knowledge of Konjic, you knew that the police building in Konjic did not have a proper detention unit and that before the war when there were more prisoners, they were taken to the prison in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, I did know that Konjic did not have a prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You indicated the size of this cell and you found 10 to 12 Serbs from the village of Celebici and its environs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you have already testified, you learnt that they had been there for some three weeks which means that they were arrested some time between 5th and 10th May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recognised Simo Jovanovic who had already been injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say that, I did not notice any visible injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did recognise him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised him and some other people who were in the cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after that, MUP members again took you to the barracks in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, Sefko Niksic, deputy chief of MUP, ordered that you be transferred there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who gave the orders for our transfer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Sefko Niksic talk to you at all on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the corridor with Jasmin Guska and with some other policemen. He said something nasty at my expense.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the conversation you had in the command building, and when you were told that you would be treated in accordance with the Geneva Convention, is it also true that you were told that you would be tried because you were with the Chetniks in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic told me I would be treated according to the Geneva Convention and that I would be tried for what I had done. I cannot recall that he said precisely what you said, that it was because I was with the Chetniks in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If this is to be found in the statement that you made for the Prosecution representative, then what you said then was not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I do not remember with precision the words used. It is quite possible that that is what he said, but he may also have said, "you will be tried for what you did", so I cannot precisely confirm whether those were the words he used.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The 3rd March school that you were transferred to the next day was adapted into some kind of an infirmary, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It might be said so, though it was not really any kind of an infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the health centre you used to work in before is not far from that school, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not far.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you probably know that in the health centre all the citizens who were injured from the shelling were treated, as well as fighters of the TO, HVO and MUP who were injured during the combat operations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The health centre is the only medical institution in the territory of the Konjic municipality, apart from the outlying infirmaries and probably whatever could be treated at that level was treated in the medical centre, all those injuries that did not require a more complicated diagnostical procedure or more complicated therapy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the persons who were in the 3rd March school were actually Serbs who were thought to have participated in the operations in Bradina and for those reasons, they were not treated in the health centre; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not so at all: it is not true at all, otherwise the conditions would have been quite different for people to be treated. There were absolutely no conditions for treating anyone, not even those injured from Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, let me ask you something else linked to your activities before the war. You remember that in Konjic, prior to the war, there were problems with medical supplies in the Konjic health centre, were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that there were any particular problems regarding medical supplies in the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But do you remember when the war began that the problem with medicines became acute in the health centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not communicate with anyone in the health centre, so I cannot confirm or deny what you are asking.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in the infirmary at the 3rd March school, you listed what you felt you needed for treatment and you sent this to the hospital pharmacy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps a couple of times at the beginning I did make a list of supplies that we needed, medicines and sterile bandages and things, syringes, antibiotics and other medicines, and I gave this to Hazim Delic. However, we would get only an insignificant amount consisting of some pain killers, some bandages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we have not understood one another. I am talking about the period of seven or eight days when you were in the 3rd March school, when, in answer to your request, you did receive a certain amount of medicines and other medical supplies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were there you were guarded together with the injured by members of the HVO police in the school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were guarded by some policemen and some military men. I do not know who they belonged to. It is possible that they were as you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And while you were there, you were able to hear strong artillery operations in town, resulting in the first civilian casualties, and some children were killed in town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that and anyway, I do not know how I could have known what was happening in town when we were isolated and locked up. We could not go out, unless opened, unlocked the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have been listening to this for four years. If I do not see anything but I can hear the shell when it hits, but you are speaking under oath and you must tell us what you think is the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The persons that you treated in the 3rd March school, to the best of your abilities, were inflicted these injuries during their arrest, transport and detention in the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And perhaps in the camp itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or probably in some other places. I cannot list all the locations where they may have been injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But if I find the statement that you made to a representative of the Prosecution in December, then your statement then was not quite correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it was not quite precise enough. I may not have mentioned that there may have been some other locations like the Celebici camp, or some other places. There were probably some other places in addition to those listed, where these people may have been injured, I could not tell, just as I cannot tell now. I could not tell then and I cannot tell now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the 3rd March school, you and the patients were not subjected to any kind of mistreatment or abuse.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have already testified, seven or eight days later you were transferred to Celebici, and immediately after your arrival you were interrogated by a commission which was conducting an investigation in connection with the Serb detainees in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not call it a commission. I was interrogated by a particular individual known as Mladen Zovko, nicknamed Kuhar. I do not know what commission he belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that other persons were interrogated too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that they were interrogated by other persons and not by Mladen Zovko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of some other people who interrogated detainees in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stenek, I cannot recall his first name, he was a teacher or a worker in MUP. Miro Stenek was his name, and some other people whose names I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They were mostly MUP personnel or inspectors of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they were people who had nothing to do with MUP who took statements, or maybe they did work for MUP. I am not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Goran Lokas was in charge of the inspectors who were conducting the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through some connections while I was still in the 3rd March school in Konjic. I learned that Goran Lokas, who used to be a head of department in MUP and for a time he was a judge because he is a lawyer by training, that he was President of the commission or whatever the function was called. Actually, he was in charge of some kind of a group that carried out some sort of investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You and your wife thought that Goran Lokas might help you because he had the authority, after examining the situation, to release individuals; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether we thought that he could release us, but we looked for ways through some connections to reach Goran Lokas, thinking that probably he might be able to help us and we knew him from before, but because of the position he held, that he might be able to help us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not succeed because Goran Lokas had a traffic accident, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that at the time the commission was joined by Jerko Kostic, also a worker in the MUP from the prewar period.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hear this name of Jerko Kostic from you for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Grubac. You have already testified that you were interrogated briefly, which questions were put to you, and that you were treated correctly while making that statement; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that they entered into that statement what you actually said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at that statement, dated 8th June 1992, to see whether you can recognise your signature on it. With the assistance of the usher I would like to show this statement to the witness, and since we received the statement from the Prosecution, I have copies here for the Trial Chamber and for the Registry. This copy is for the witness. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D59/1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, will you please look at the signature on the second page. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to look at the right-hand corner of the first page. There is "4K" written. Can you tell me whether you know that prisoners were classified into several categories in our language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that prisoners were categorised, but I do not know what the system was nor how many categories there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If it says "4K" on the top of the page, does that mean that you belong to the fourth category?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the person who interrogated you, or who it was that analysed whatever you said, established that you belonged to the fourth category?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could I know that? It probably does mean that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the fact that the witness confirmed the content of the statement, and also recognised his signature on the statement, that this statement be admitted as evidence of the Defence, D/51.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Grubac, you said that about mid June an injured Pero Mrkajic was brought to the infirmary, and that he died in the infirmary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Dr. Grubac, that a group of inhabitants of Bradina tried to cross into Serb held territory in the direction of Kalinovik and that they were later arrested and brought into custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that this group of prisoners was mistreated and beaten fiercely while being arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some members of that group told me as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you also aware that Pero Mrkajic was among one of those subsequently brought in groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Grubac, we can now pass on to another subject that you have testified to before this Trial Chamber. Actually, in answer to my question you said that for a time you performed the duties of director of the health centre in Konjic. While you held that post, did you have the authority to pass on some of your competencies to someone else when you were unable to perform your duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that six or seven days prior to your release from Celebici, your wife came to visit, your wife Gordana?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If your wife Gordana said in a statement to a representative of the International Tribunal that she visited you the day before your release, then she was not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She probably remembers better than I do. It may have been one day -- I do not understand, what did I say, ten days?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, you said seven or eight days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Her statement is probably more correct than mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your wife was living in Konjic with her parents throughout the time you spent in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that when you met with your wife, you asked her to go and see your best man from your wedding, Dr. Ahmed Jusufbegovic, and to ask him if he could to bring about your release?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, after she left you did not know whether she had contacted Dr. Jusufbegovic or whether she had tried to help you in some other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not know, nor did I know whether she had contacted Dr. Jusufbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you were informed the next day that you and Dr. Relja would be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought it was several days later, but probably it was the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that same evening, about 9.00 pm, a guard known as Focak came and said jokingly that you had reason to treat people and he gave you the release papers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The paper that you were given was addressed to you and it was signed, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you were taken to Mr. Delalic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, the release paper contained everything that we have already seen and no corrections were made on that document in your presence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall such details, whether anything was added to that document or not. I cannot claim that the content of that paper was the same when we received it in Celebici or whether Zejnil or somebody else added anything to it in his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if this morning during the examination-in-chief you said that a correction may have been made on the papers of Dr. Relja, then you were not saying the precise truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I said that I was not sure what was added to those papers. It is possible that something may have been added on Relja's because he asked another location to be indicated, but I did not exclude the possibility of anything being added on my paper. It is something I simply cannot remember. I cannot claim that anything was added or that was not added. I cannot be quite definite about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During that brief visit to Mr. Delalic's home, you were able to see that Mr. Delalic was surprised that you were a prisoner in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Talking to Mr. Delalic were you able to notice his surprise that you were a prisoner in the Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not my impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a third party would say that, then that is their impression, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I really could not gain such an impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask the usher's assistance to show you an exhibit of the Prosecution, I think it is number 69, your release paper, if we can look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 169.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, in the lower right-hand corner is it true that you see the word "head of the investigating body".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That cannot be seen clearly on my copy, but I think -- can I look at this copy? Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that after that heading, you see the small word "for" in handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grubac, in addition to having heard that Goran Lokas was President or head of that body while you were in the 3rd March school, did you know who headed the investigating body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know at all that such a position existed. I did not even know that there was an investigating body, because nobody did any investigations apart from these statements, and I did not even know that Goran Lokas was in charge of that investigating body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Dr. Grubac, but if you see that above the title you see the word "for", this would mean that the person signing the document was not the person heading the investigating body.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what that means, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But let us try and simplify matters a little. Since you were the director and you already told me that you could authorise somebody orally or in writing to do something on your behalf, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one of the doctors or employees received such authority, then also before signing a paper of any kind they would have to add the small word "for" or "on behalf of" the manager. That would be the procedure for signing the document on your behalf.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you will agree with me, generally speaking, that if there is such a word "for" attached to a signature it indicates that the person signing the document is doing so upon the authority of somebody else or on behalf of somebody else; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, let me ask you this: did you know that at the time when you were released, in the area towards Boracko Lake there was combat, there was an offensive on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know of any such activities, of any offensive against Celebici when I was released.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not Celebici, the Boracko Lake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not on Boracko Lake and I do not see how you could think I would know of such an offensive.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me refresh your memory Mr. Grubac a bit. That evening when you came to Mr. Delalic's, you found out that he had just come from the combat positions from Vranske Stijene that he had to return soon after, that he had just come from combat. Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember at all of his having told me that he had taken part in any combat. I, in fact, thought that he did not take part in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Dr. Relja Mrkajic says that Zejnil Delalic had precisely come on that day from some combat position, then you feel he is not saying the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no reason not to tell the truth. I just want to tell you that I do not remember Zejnil telling us that he had come from any combat positions. This is the first time I hear of such a formulation. It is possible that Relja in some contact with him, while I was perhaps doing something else, heard that particular piece of information. I am not saying that it is not true, but I cannot confirm it because I really do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, when you were recognising this model during the examination-in-chief as the model of the Celebici barracks, you pointed to the buildings which were used as a prison at the camp, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you probably know that this entire compound has some 10,000 square metres of overall area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that practically only a small part of this entire space was used as a camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you certainly know that a large part of the building was used to house equipment, armaments, food for the area of the entire Bosnia and other material and supplies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of it from you. I had no idea for what purposes it was being used and what was the use of the rest of the facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in this facility there were large warehouses of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that either. These were probably some secrets and I do not see why you think, and how you think that I could have known what was in the military warehouses there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And any vehicle which entered the compound of the barracks of Celebici had to pass through this first gate which you have indicated to us, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether that is so. Perhaps in addition to that road leading to the railway and that entrance there was some other entrance perhaps also. I do not know of one and I had no way of knowing if there had been one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But during your sojourn there, did you see numerous trucks and other vehicles passing on that road through the gate in front of number 9 to the farther areas of the barracks, of the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never saw such trucks. I did hear from some prisoners, they said that some trucks had come, that they had unloaded some armaments, ammunitions and so on, but I personally never saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if you heard from the prisoners that armaments and other supplies had been unloaded, then you probably can confirm that that meant that the Celebici barracks, not the camp, that many people connected by business ties and associated with the camp compound because of the other activities within the compound had to come to the camp, you can agree on that score with me, can you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a different assumption, because first you advance this first assumption from which you derive this second assumption. Theoretically I could agree with you, but I cannot confirm that. There are too many assumptions in your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, I would really like you to answer to the best of your knowledge and for me not to have a single assumption in my questions, but I asked my question on the basis of your answer, that you were told by prisoners that they had unloaded ammunition and armaments and other supplies there and I thought that that was a fact which was known to you, and my question was based on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I tell you that here in court, the stories are not taken for facts because in that case I could adduce as many facts as I could think of, but these are stories, accounts of other people which are not accepted by the court as facts and that is why I answered in the way in which I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grubac, you said that you knew personally the family of Zejnil Delalic, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some members of his family, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know his brothers and some relatives of his, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are, if I can put it that way, the family doctor of this family; you treated his mother and his brother, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can certainly testify before this Tribunal that some members of this family are very similar to each other, Zejnil, Zajka and the late Sefik who you also treated for instance, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they resemble each other very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And people who, like you yourself, do not know them well, could probably substitute one of them for the other, could they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not myself substitute one of them for the other, but I do believe that some people could do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You used to meet the late Sefik in the Celebici barracks also and on a couple of occasions he also assisted you financially, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grubac, you also know Jasna Dzumhur who was the chairwoman of the exchange commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I know her. I also knew her before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that in discharging her duties, Jasna also used a Jeep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that, I hear of it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But do you know that at that time, Mr. Delalic had two jeeps, a white one and a green one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had a number of Jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that in view of the war circumstances and everything that was going on there, his brothers Dzemal and his relatives and his drivers often drove those jeeps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know for a fact that his late brother Sefik drove one of those Jeeps, the second Jeep.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the location of the building number 22, which is to say right across the administrative building, as you said, you could sometimes see vehicles being parked in front of that administrative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you probably know that people who came on various businesses to Celebici also dropped in at the command building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you can agree with me that at the time when you saw one of the jeeps driven by Zejnil, that did not necessarily mean that Zejnil was in the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know that during the war Mr. Delalic engaged in various logistic transactions, and if he did come to the barracks that that could have been connected with that particular purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to repeat that I had no idea of the kind of business that Zejnil was engaged in, whether he was in logistic or any other activities. It was only -- for the first time that I saw his function written on one of these papers when I visited his house with my wife, when I saw his title written on one of these papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have testified before this court, that was in mid September or somewhere around that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since when have you known Mr. Delalic, Mr. Grubac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not say exactly. I think I have known him for a long time, starting many years before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know that he lived abroad for quite a number of years, and occasionally only came to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you also know that as a well to do affluent citizen, he helped in Konjic various sports and cultural events, activities, the regatta on the lake, boat race and similar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as a doctor and the health centre manager, you also know that he financially helped the health centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that he donated to the health centre when it was in troubled times, and I believe that his intentions were good and that he intended to help genuinely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You probably know that immediately prior to the war, because of the problems with the dialysis of those patients who had to be on such apparata, he procured haemodialysis apparatus for the health centre which unfortunately due to the circumstances was never connected and used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hear this for the first time, but I do know that before that he helped us provide and procure some equipment for the health centre. I have not heard of this particular apparatus and that is probably because at that time I could no longer have any contact with the health centre. I think he did such things because this is something which was like him, was not alien to him, but I cannot confirm it. I do not know it for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But as a friend, perhaps, I could say a family friend of the Delalics, you knew that during the war he held neither political nor state function or office in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that he held neither a political nor any state office in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But he had the reputation of a good businessman and a well to do citizen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in a small town many people actually felt honoured to be in his society, in his company; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that many people really liked to stick around him and that they liked to be seen in his company, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even some people who were not in his company liked to brag down town how close to him they were; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Grubac, Zejnil Delalic is a friend of yours, but also because he is held in very high esteem, your attitude as a doctor towards the members of his family, especially towards his brother, had been prepared even before to pay you back in various ways for your services; is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And irrespective of the war and the ethnic tensions which emerged, at the moment when you met with Mr. Delalic it was quite clear to you that Mr. Delalic had not changed his attitude towards you; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It seemed to me that he had not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you heard at the time that between Bradina and Jablanica there was a mini-railway which started to operate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I even believe that they call it "Zejnil's railway".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that he used significant personal funds and a lot of his time to make it easier for the people to pass these distances, to cover these distances under those war circumstances; you have heard that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, probably the very fact that they call it Zejnil's railway probably means that his role in it, in its starting to operate, was indeed prominent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew that this railway was used by all the people without charge and the women in Bradina who wanted to see their loved ones in Celebici could use this railway as a safer way to reach Celebici, there was no discrimination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you also knew that there were many people gossiping about Zejnil in Konjic, wagging their tongues, and that some even harboured a hostile attitude to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some rumours were bandied about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now you have verified your relationship, your attitude towards Mr. Zejnil Delalic better, when you were about to leave your wife told you that it had been her idea when she saw that Zejnil was in Konjic to address him, counting on this friendship of yours; is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the reason why we had opted for her going to see precisely Zejnil and, secondly, we also thought he was in a position to do something for us, that he was a person who could do something for us if he wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am talking about your release, so her addressing Zejnil in connection with your release was the idea of your wife, because you had told her to see Dr. Jusufbegovic, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have described quite well the position of the house of Mr. Delalic, but I should only like to ask you, is it true that this house is under a high cut in the rock and that it is in a relatively safe place vis-a-vis the shelling which was quite intensive at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that it is in a safe place. Across from it there is this cut in the rock and this house was sheltered by this hill which was on the opposite side from the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During these two visits to Mr. Delalic's house and probably while you were staying in Konjic, you found out personally that in the basement of Mr. Delalic's house there was housed a communication centre of the headquarters of the Territorial Defence of the commune of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is something I hear for the first time now. Evidently you think that I was much better informed than I actually was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection to your visits with Mr. Mucic to Celebici, you said that Mucic at the time on the way would visit Mr. Delalic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both times he went to Mr. Zejnil Delalic's house on the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed in the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see who Mucic met with in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no way we could see that and we do not know whom he met with in the house, nor whom he went to see inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nor did Mucic tell you on what business he would go inside the house, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not, he never told us why he was going into the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grubac, you were also in Celebici at the time the international committee of the Red Cross visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not in Celebici at the time when it was visited by the International Red Cross. I had been released. That was in August, August 12th, I think, but I was conditionally speaking released in parole.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but when you returned from this recess, you could notice that the situation in the camp, in the prison had significantly improved, had it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it had. The situation had significantly improved after the visit of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for recognising the position to stop. We will continue with you tomorrow morning. (5.35 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day) 21 22 23 24 25
